label: End-of-episode clock at GO (late trials, biased toward choosing a2)
explanation: Fires almost only at GO (99.9% of mass) and only in the final ~13 trials of the 100-trial episode: never before trial ~80, 9x lift in trials 90-99. Magnitude ramps up with episode trial (activations in a window rise steadily trial by trial; the top quartile is 99.9% within trials >= 90). It tracks the low value the model predicts near the episode end: (GO & value < 5.22) alone gives F1 0.84. The agent cannot see the trial index, so this is an internally kept clock. In trials ~86-92 it fires mainly when the agent is about to choose a2 (86% of mass is on a2 choices); from about trial 93 on it fires for both actions. The recorded predicate uses the agent own GO policy argmax (model_act), which it computes and does not depend on a future outcome. Reward, transition, stay/switch, and the good state have no effect (lift about 1x). It does not fire at D1 or D2. Simpler alternatives: GO & ep_trial >= 88 gives F1 0.79 and mass recall 0.98.

issues: The reported test scores reproduce exactly: P 0.816, R 0.935, F1 0.872, mass recall 0.978. GO-only holds: GO carries 0.999 of the activation mass. The trial claims hold: 0 activations in trials 0-69 and only 2 in trials 70-79. Top-quartile coverage for ep_trial>=90 is 0.999. The value predicate (GO & value<5.22) scores test F1 0.856. Reward, common transition, stay and core_pattern all have lift around 1x.
Small understatement: in trials 86-92, 96.5% of the dev mass is on model_act==2 choices, not the 86% the explanation gives.

The a1/a2 split is graded, not a step at trial 93. The share of GO steps that are active, by trial: a2 choices 0.20 at t86, 0.52 at t88, 0.85 at t90, 0.95 at t92; a1 choices 0.25 at t92, 0.54 at t94, 0.85 at t96, 0.98 at t98. So a1 onset lags a2 by about 6 trials, and the strength of the a2 preference matters too, not just the argmax. Most of the 7283 test false positives are this boundary: a1 choices around trials 93-95 and weak-a2 trials around 87-89. Scoring the choice logit as a continuous amount captures it (test F1 0.889 vs 0.872). This is a refinement, not a missing class.

in_rew==-1 (failed D1 fixation) has 21x lift, but all of those activations are late in the episode (0 active before trial 80). The late-trial clock already covers them, so there is no separate penalty feature.
The predicate's model_act is the agent's own computed choice. Swapping in the actual action gives the same F1 (0.872), and no future random outcome is involved. The label does not overclaim.
